title: Reels-RSI: Program-Level Self-Improvement for Code-Rendered Explainer Videos
abstract: arXiv:2610.14495v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Explainer videos -- a worked geometry problem, why the sky is blue, how a dynasty fell -- are usually one more target for pixel video generation. We argue they are a different kind of artifact: a program (script, storyboard and per-frame animation code) that a deterministic renderer turns into frames. A program can be read, diffed, tested and audited; pixels can only be watched. Reels-RSI is an open-source reel director for any agent harness; its self-improvement happens at the program level rather than in weights or prompts. Every revision pass is logged with a code snapshot; a retrospective pairs each check finding with the diff that fixed it and proposes lessons; a lesson that a static check can catch is compiled into a rule with a must-fail and a must-pass example, so the memory is unit-tested; and a rule learned today runs over everything made before it. A bounded, benchmark-gated step lets an agent rewrite the director's playbook,

translated_title: Reels-RSI：面向代码渲染讲解视频的程序级自我改进
translated_abstract: 讲解视频——比如一道几何例题的完整解题过程、天空为什么是蓝色的、一个王朝是如何覆灭的——通常只是像素视频生成的又一个应用目标。我们认为它们是另一种性质的产物：一个程序（脚本、分镜脚本和逐帧动画代码），由确定性渲染器将其转换为帧画面。程序可以被阅读、对比（diff）、测试和审计；而像素只能被观看。Reels-RSI 是一个开源的短视频导演系统，可接入任何智能体框架；它的自我改进发生在程序层面，而不是权重或提示词层面。每一次修订过程都伴随代码快照被完整记录；一次复盘会将每条检查发现与修复它的代码差异配对，并提炼出经验教训；凡是静态检查能捕捉到的经验教训，都会被编译成一条规则，并附带一个必须失败的示例和一个必须通过的示例，因此记忆是经过单元测试的；今天学到的规则还会回溯运行于此前创作的所有作品之上。一个有界的、以基准测试为门槛的步骤，允许智能体重写导演的操作手册，
tldr: 该论文提出开源系统 Reels-RSI，将讲解视频视为可阅读、可测试、可审计的程序而非像素，通过“检查发现—修复差异—提炼教训—编译为带单元测试的规则—回溯应用于历史作品”的程序级自我改进闭环，让智能体在基准测试门槛约束下不断重写导演手册，从而持续提升讲解视频的创作质量。
en_tdlr: Reels-RSI is an open-source "reel director" that treats explainer videos as programs (script, storyboard, and per-frame animation code) rather than pixels, enabling program-level self-improvement where every revision is logged with code snapshots, retrospectives pair check findings with fixing diffs, lessons are compiled into unit-tested rules that retroactively apply to past work, and a benchmark-gated step lets the agent rewrite its own director's playbook.
